findings.where: First screen, desktop and phone: the hero frame (logo, name, nav, Mark's line, supporting paragraph, portrait), and the nav bar (Profile, Articles, Blog)
findings.fault: The page has no way to reach Mark. No email address is shown, there is no contact link anywhere on the page (parts.txt lists only the home link, three nav anchors, one PDF link and the replay button), and the nav has no Contact item. The palette says pad yellow is for 'the address strip', and the texture note puts the address 'at the foot of the sheet'. Neither appears on the first screen or anywhere else, so the yellow shows up only in the specimen swatches.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank staffer who has just read Mark's line and wants to write to him finds no address and no action, and has to go and look for him elsewhere. The founder's test asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark with the address shown, and getting in touch is the page's one job.

findings.where: Motion sketch panel, desktop-04/05 and phone-03/04: the lilac ground behind the curve, the replayed line and the timing table
findings.fault: A large field of lilac/purple, a hue that is not in the declared four-colour palette, fills the biggest single block below the fold. The palette's own note says the purple stage backdrop 'turns to ink' so that blue and grey are the only ink. Blue links and the blue curve also sit on this purple, a pairing the palette never planned.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for every tile to be built in or around the house blue and grey, with one soft ground and no other hue. The purple reads as a stray colour from another brand and undercuts the restraint the tile claims.

findings.where: Article specimen subheads: 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' and 'Download', desktop-04 and phone-03
findings.fault: The subheads use a third typeface, a heavy, wide grotesque. It is neither of the declared pair (the type-pair card says subheads are Newsreader 500), and it is much louder and blunter than the light serif voice of the rest of the page.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and later editors, because the specimen gives no single, stated subhead style for her to follow. The founder too, who asked for serious, refined type with nothing in-your-face: the black grotesque shouts within a quiet legal-journal page.

findings.where: Article specimen headline 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law', desktop-03 and phone-02
findings.fault: The article title is set in a heavy, bold serif. That weight is not in the type pair as declared (Light 300 display, Regular 400 text, 500 subheads), and it breaks from the light display serif of the hero line. The two headline levels look like they come from two different systems.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging whether the article page and homepage read as one identity. A reader moving from the light, quiet hero to a bold, poster-weight article title feels a change of voice.

findings.where: Palette section swatches, desktop-02 and phone-01
findings.fault: Each of the four swatches has a different shape and edge: a square with a hairline, a rounded filled rectangle, an outlined ellipse, and a rectangle with a thick blue border. The yellow swatch's blue border reads like a selected or focused state, not a colour sample.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the palette as a specimen. The mixed treatments suggest meanings (rounded, oval, selected) that the colours do not have, and they contradict the tile's 'square at every corner' frame rule.

findings.where: Article specimen 'Download' row into the motion panel, desktop-04 bottom and phone-03
findings.fault: The PDF link and its 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' line sit hard against the top of the lilac motion panel, with no space between them. The article's last item looks attached to the next section, and the article has no real ending. On desktop the meta line also floats far right, away from the title it describes.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning the article for its downloads, which the research names as the product. The Download item runs into an unrelated panel, so where the article ends is unclear, and the date is split from its title.

findings.where: Article specimen Download link 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge'
findings.fault: The one publication link goes to '#', so it leads nowhere. It also offers a bare PDF with no HTML page in front of it, though the trust rules ask for each publication to have its own page with the PDF behind it.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who wants to check Mark's work. Publications are the proof an advisor is judged by, and this one cannot be opened or read on the site.

findings.where: Texture specimen box, desktop-02/03 and phone-02
findings.fault: The texture sample is an empty hairline box with a part-width yellow band along its bottom. It reads like a loading or progress bar, not a sheet of paper with an address strip.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who is asked to judge the ground's busyness and border placement from this sample. It does not show what it describes.

findings.fault: A button that acts in place is styled exactly like a prose link (blue, underlined), which is the signifier reserved for navigation.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects an underlined blue link to take them somewhere; few would mind on a specimen panel, but it sets a pattern that conflicts with the article's real links.
